s.t:
Spreedly is the world's leading Open Payments Platform. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in Durham, NC, the company gives mid-market and enterprise businesses the infrastructure to connect to any payment gateway, processor, or fraud tool through a single API. The platform is vendor-agnostic by design, meaning customers are never locked into a single provider and never need to rebuild their payments stack to access new capabilities.
The core business problem Spreedly solves is real and costly: global merchants face a fragmented payments ecosystem, where every new market, payment method, or fraud tool typically requires a separate, time-consuming integration. Spreedly eliminates that complexity, enabling companies to route transactions intelligently, secure cardholder data, prevent fraud, and expand into new markets without heavy engineering overhead.

As a Technical Program Manager , you will be a key player in our pre-sales and customer solutioning efforts. You will partner closely with Account Executives, Product, and Engineering to scope technical solutions that align with customer needs and drive Spreedly's growth. This is a customer-facing, consultative role focused on understanding prospect pain points and designing solutions that connect Spreedly's platform capabilities to business outcomes.
You will also influence revenue growth, shorten time-to-close, and accelerate value realization for our customers. As Spreedly scales, this role will shape our go-to-market infrastructure through solution templates, demo assets, and mentoring, making it an ideal opportunity for impact and professional growth.
This is a US-based customer-facing role supporting primarily US customers and cross-functional teams operating within US business hours. Success in this role requires regular travel within the United States and the ability to work in alignment with US customer and internal stakeholder schedules.

Lead technical discovery sessions with prospects and customers to identify needs and align use cases to Spreedly's capabilities
Deliver compelling demos, architecture diagrams, and documentation that support sales conversations and technical evaluation
Translate business and technical requirements into actionable solution proposals and implementation plans that support scalability and reuse
Develop and maintain reusable demo environments, solution artifacts, and objection handling templates
Work with Product and Engineering teams to provide prospect feedback and ensure solution feasibility
Partner with Customer Success and Support teams to ensure smooth implementation handoffs
Serve as a technical expert in RFPs, security reviews, and compliance questionnaires
Educate internal teams on platform capabilities, integration patterns, and sales enablement materials

3+ years in a Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, or Technical Account Manager role within a B2B SaaS or fintech environment
Industry experience with eCommerce, PSPs, payment orchestration, or payment platforms
Background in payments, card-not-present commerce, fraud, or gateways preferred
Strong knowledge of APIs, SDKs, and system integration principles (especially REST and webhooks)
Familiarity with scripting or backend programming (Python, Ruby, or JavaScript a plus)
Experience collaborating with Sales and Product teams on enterprise deals
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including customer-facing documentation
Ability to simplify complex technical topics and guide customer decision-making

Comfortable owning discovery and demo stages in an enterprise sales motion
Experience with implementation or support functions is a plus

Outstanding Medical and Dental benefits, including 100% employer-paid options
Company-paid Life and Disability insurance
Optional vision and supplemental insurance options, and various Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)

Access to company-paid professional coaching service
Visits to HQ in Durham, North Carolina for remote employees
Additional Information

Spreedly provides an open payments platform. The platform’s connectivity provides payments performance. Key products and services include:
Connect — A unified API that integrates with hundreds of payment gateways, processors, and alternative payment methods worldwide, including digital wallets. Merchants access the global payments ecosystem through one connection.
Vault — A PCI-compliant secure repository for payment methods. Merchants store card data once and reuse it across any payment service, reducing PCI scope and protecting cardholder data at scale.
Optimize — Workflow-driven routing and retry logic that directs each transaction to the best-performing gateway in real time. On average, 7.9% of failed transactions succeed immediately when retried on a secondary gateway. This is where merchants recover lost revenue and increase authorization success rates.
Protect — A flexible fraud and authentication layer, incorporating advanced fraud tools and 3DS. Following Spreedly's acquisition of Dodgeball in September 2025, fraud orchestration and payment optimization now operate within the same platform.
Resolve — Centralized management and reporting that reduces operational silos, strengthens security, and improves billing control across a merchant's entire payment operation.
More Coming Soon! - Keep your eyes peeled for a new product launch by EOY '26

s.h: What It's Like to Work Here
s.t:
We describe our team as "Spreedlings": diverse, forward-thinking, and driven by a shared belief that a more open payments ecosystem benefits everyone. The company operates with a culture built on transparency, courageous collaboration, and self-driven leadership. The team values simplicity in both product and process, and approaches problem-solving with genuine curiosity.
--
We champion the ethical, creative use of AI—if you’re someone who pairs human judgment with modern AI tools to work smarter and drive bigger impact, you’ll thrive here.
--
Spreedly is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering, cultivating, and preserving a culture of diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging. We actively work to drive out even unintentional discrimination in our hiring processes via practices like blindly graded work samples, structured interviews, and diversity awareness training.
Due to the sensitive nature of what Spreedly does - handling payment data - finalist candidates must complete a successful background and reference check.
At this time Spreedly is unable to provide sponsorship for employment, and we are not set up to support remote employees who reside in New York. In order to be considered for employment, applicants must be currently legally authorized to work in the job location country and not require future sponsorship in order to continue working in that country.

Amazon Extra Large (AMXL) is a single-threaded organization that owns the end-to-end customer experience for heavy and bulky products, from supply chain and fulfillment through transportation, last mile delivery, and post-purchase resolution. AMXL currently operates across North America, Europe, Japan, and is expanding into emerging markets.

Within AMXL, the CX and Growth org is a centralized, worldwide team organized across five pillars designed to ensure that every customer who purchases a large, high-value product receives a reliable experience.
The Execution Excellence pillar is where planning meets the customer. It houses two complementary teams: our AMXL Operations Center and our AMXL Proactive Execution program.

These teams serve as the real-time network execution backbone, translating strategic decisions into daily network performance across our end-to-end network and also as the mechanism that identifies delivery failures before they become visible to the customer and intervenes proactively to save the delivery or manage the recovery directly with the customer.

Together, these teams form a closed loop: detect upstream, prevent where possible, intervene proactively where not, and feed root causes back so defects are resolved at the source.
We are seeking a Senior Program Manager to lead the integration and transformation of this combined organization. This is not a steady-state program management role. The program strategy is being built.

You will inherit a consolidation in progress and own the lifecycle of making it work: assessing what the combined org should look like, defining how we measure success, building the mechanisms that make it sustainable, and driving the hard conversations required to get there.

You will use process lifecycle evaluation methodologies to categorize the team's portfolio (automate, simplify, reallocate, or deprecate), and build automation roadmaps in partnership with technical teams.
This role requires someone who can operate in high ambiguity, make trade-offs between short-term operational needs and long-term strategic goals, and communicate persuasively across teams. The right candidate sees automation and AI as something they use today, not something they plan to use later, and will set the standard for how this team uses technology to scale impact without scaling headcount.

· Define the operating model for the combined organization: org design, process rationalization, scope definition, and mechanisms that make it self-sustaining.
· Build the process lifecycle evaluation framework, determining which workflows to automate, simplify, reallocate, or retire, and manage the pipeline of new use cases from scoping through launch.
· Own the automation roadmap in partnership with data science, engineering, and technology teams, establishing accountability mechanisms with clear timelines for every manual process.
· Drive cross-functional stakeholder alignment across supply chain, quality, and operations, navigating complex organizational dynamics and building trust where needed.
· Scale this capability into new geographies by adapting the operating model to local carrier ecosystems, regulatory environments, and workforce availability.
A day in the life
You might start your morning reviewing program metrics dashboards, identifying areas that need attention, and preparing a status narrative for a director-level review. By mid-morning you are facilitating a working session with partners to align on priorities for the quarter.

After lunch you dive into data to validate assumptions behind a proposed solution, then draft a decision document that frames trade-offs for leadership. You close the day mentoring a newer program manager and connecting with cross-regional counterparts to keep workstreams on track.

The AMXL Customer Experience and Growth team takes a 360-degree approach to the customer journey:
· **Eliminate**: detect, solve, and resolve customer-impacting issues upstream by providing relevant and timely insights for operations teams, transportation, and product development.
· **Automate**: continuously assess and identify opportunities to replace manual processes with automated, scalable solutions.
· **Optimize**: when a customer does need support, ensure AMXL stakeholders have the tools, resources, policies, and protocols to deliver a perfect experience.
The operations center translates strategic decisions into daily network performance. The proactive execution team ensures that when defects occur, customers are protected through early intervention. The Sr. Program Manager will be the link that makes both teams operate as one system.

About Focused Energy
Focused Energy is building the future of clean energy through laser-driven inertial fusion. Backed by our $240M Series A - the largest fully secured Series A in the global fusion industry we are scaling rapidly across multiple geographies.
Based in Germany and the US, we have brought together the top scientific and engineering minds using proven technologies to unlock fusion power at commercial scale. Focused Energy is working to realize game-changing scientific innovation that promises to deliver a clean, sustainable and abundant source of power globally.
As a Program Manager - Reactor you will be responsible for managing the reactor department projects and coordinate with other departments and aligning with company wide PM efforts.

Plan and track projects, translating strategic goals into clear tasks, schedules, and milestones with particular emphasis on long-horizon, high-consequence programs such as the fusion island wall design, procurement and commissioning.
Track budget and personnel capacity to ensure efficient resource allocation across multi-year reactor programs.
Maintain project plans, schedules, and workflows in Jira, Jira Big Picture and Confluence.
Track progress and follow up with engineers and stakeholders from reactor, engineering, targets, lasers and science.
Planning and coordination of appointments, meetings, sessions, and events such as conferences, safety reviews, and internal progress review days, including follow-up on decisions and action items.
Own risk and change management as a core responsibility; maintain risk registers, drive mitigation planning, and ensure change control processes are followed rigorously in a safety-critical environment.
Serve as the central point of contact for interfacing with program management, finance, and all other SST departments; liaise with suppliers, research partners, external regulatory bodies and government partners where applicable.
Coordinate with company-wide PM efforts to ensure compliance with company-wide standards.
Support public funding resource coordination with our finance and programs team.
Ensure adherence to radiation safety, high-voltage system protocols, and any applicable nuclear regulatory or licensing requirements; coordinate with safety officers and compliance leads as needed

Master's degree or higher in nuclear engineering, physics, or a related field; a PhD preferred.
Deep experience in R&D and engineering-heavy project management and coordination, ideally within experimental physics or nuclear energy research environments.
Strong communication, administrative, and personal time-management skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in both English and German.

We have an excitingopportunity for a Technical Program Manager atUL Research Institutes, within our Digital Safety Research Institute (DSRI). This isa REMOTE opportunity
The Technical Program Manager plans, executes, and brings projects to closure on behalf of Digital Safety. The Technical Program Manager oversees the entire technical project lifecycle, ensuring that projects are completed on time, within budget, and according to the specified scope and quality requirements. The Technical Program Manager manages resources, coordinates teams, and mitigates risks to deliver successful project outcomes.

AtUL Research Institutes(ULRI),weexpand the boundaries of safety science tocreate a more secure and sustainable world. Formore thana century, we have studied the unintended consequences of innovation, designed solutions to mitigateriskand shared our findings with academia, scientists, manufacturers, and policymakers across industries.Weidentifycritical safety and sustainability issues, askingtoughquestions because we believe a safer world begins with knowledge.
Build a safer, more secure, and sustainable future with us.Join us and work with our Fire Safetyteamswho conduct the researchrequiredto produce that knowledgeandput itintopractice.

The Digital Safety Research Institute (DSRI) addresses unresolved safety risks and emerging dangers in the world’s digital ecosystem. We aim to help protect people from unwanted access to personal devices and privacy,algorithms, and disinformation threats by working to create a new digital safety ecosystem.
DSRI is committed to sharing digital safety insights, collaborating with key stakeholders, and offering extensive outreach and education to help support safer digital environments for people everywhere.

As the Technical Program Manager, youwill play a key role in the rapid growth ofULas you:
Define projectobjectives, scope, deliverables, and success criteria and develop comprehensive project plans, including schedules, budgets, and resource allocation,Identifyingproject dependencies, risks, and mitigation strategies.
Collaborate with engineering team leads, research leadership, and external partners (sponsors, researchers, engineers, and adopters) to gather requirements andestablishclear communication channels.
Coordinate and lead cross-functional project teams, assign tasks and responsibilities, and monitor project progress, ensuring adherence to timelines, budgets, and quality standards. Foster effective teamwork and collaboration among team members.
Conduct regular project status meetings, providing updates to stakeholders and addressing any issues or concerns.
Manage changes to project scope, schedule, and resources, followingappropriate changecontrol processes and proactivelyidentifyand resolve project issues and conflicts.
Escalate critical risks and issues toappropriate stakeholdersand senior management.
Ensure compliance with organizational policies, sponsor requirements, research data-handling expectations, andour open-source release processes.
Establishandmaintainstrong relationships with project stakeholders, ensuring effective communication and collaboration. and provide regular project status reports and updates to stakeholders, including progress, milestones, and key decisions.
Manage resources to balance internal Digital Safety tasks with UL-wide organizational assignments.
Manage stakeholder expectations and address concerns or feedback.
Facilitateeffective communication among project team members, ensuring alignment and clarity.
Conduct project reviews andlessonslearned sessions toidentifyareas for improvement.
Document project outcomes, successes, and challenges for future reference.

In short
We're looking for a Senior Project Manager to join our PM team and lead mobile and web projects for IoT, wearables, and connected devices. You'll be the single point of contact for our US-based clients and the person holding a cross-functional team together day to day. This is a permanent role: B2B contract, monthly salary, full benefits, and a team that has been doing this since 2008.
Why intent ?
We've been designing and co-creating connected devices since 2008. Wearables, smart audio, health-tech hardware for clients like Oura and BOSE, backed by investors like a16z and Founders Fund. We're 60+ people, fully remote, and AI-native since before LinkedIn influencers discovered the term. Our PMs don't manage Jira tickets, they own projects: scoping, staffing, client conversations, trade-offs, and the day-to-day rhythm that makes a connected product actually ship.
Who this role is NOT for
If you like running stand-ups by the book, sending status updates, and waiting for someone else to make the hard calls, we're probably not your people. We look for PMs who ask "why" before "how", challenge specs that don't add up, and walk into a room full of ambiguity ready to create structure.

We're AI-native and we expect you to treat AI as a daily multiplier, not a gimmick. What we expect: ownership of your project end to end, straight talk with clients and the team, and the kind of curiosity that makes you actually care about what the device does, not just whether the sprint closes on time.

Be the single point of contact for our US-based clients: great communicator, diplomat, and when needed, negotiator
Manage web and mobile projects end to end: discovery, scoping, launch, and what comes after
Lead a cross-functional squad of designers, developers, QA, and other PMs
Run Scrum ceremonies, plan sprints, manage backlogs, timelines, budgets, and project health
Co-create product vision with clients: features, MVP strategy, the smartest way to deliver value
Lead staffing and resource planning with other chapters
Push for better ways of working, inside your squad and across the company
Use AI tools as part of your daily workflow, not as a party trick
How we work
Fully remote. We have a pet-friendly office in Warsaw and a coworking space in Gdansk if walls and coffee machines motivate you, but nobody will ask why you're not there. Working hours are flexible: most of the team operates between 10:00 and 18:00 CET, and that's when most meetings happen.

Evening calls with US-based clients (typically 16:00-20:00 CET, around 2-3 per week) are a normal part of the PM role here, always planned ahead. You'll be part of the PM chapter for knowledge-sharing, and at the same time leading your own project squad day to day.
What you'll get

s.h: 17,000-23,000 PLN/month net B2B, depending on your experience
s.t:
26 days of paid leave
10 days of paid sick leave
Saltus medical care
Self-development budget (2,000 PLN or 500 USD/year)

All necessary equipment provided

Your first months
We aim to give you space to ramp up before owning a full project, but this is a real company with real deadlines: if a squad needs you sooner, we'll make sure you have the support to hit the ground running. You'll get paired with a buddy, meet the team, and start with real tasks while being guided by your team and leadership.

Monthly HR check-ins, real feedback after month two, and a proper review after month three: if things feel great on both sides, you're officially part of the crew. No one waits three months to tell you something isn't working: if it's great, you'll know; if something needs adjusting, you'll hear about it while there's still time to adjust.

The entire process is in English. All interviews are recorded for internal evaluation purposes.

Once we're in touch, you'll hear from us fast. We don't ghost and we don't drag.
One more thing
intent is an equal opportunity employer. We care about what you can do, not where you come from. Send us your CV and a few words about why this caught your eye. Bonus points if you share a project you led that you're proud of, ideally one where the delivery was harder than the spec suggested.

As an IT Program Manager (Service Designer), GS-2210-15, you will be responsible for: Leading discovery and design efforts rooted in empathy for students, families, and financial aid administrators. Ensuring FSA services are intuitive and accessible to users of all backgrounds, and that every interaction builds trust and confidence in the program.

Looking beyond the screen to understand and improve the end-to-end journey of applying for and receiving aid, mapping processes, policies, and touchpoints across agencies and partners, identifying pain points and opportunities for more seamless, equitable services.

Designing solutions that account for the full ecosystem, not just individual transactions. Leading usability testing with diverse users, incorporating feedback into design iterations. Ensuring that final solutions can scale to millions of FSA users while maintaining clarity, accessibility, and reliability.

Championing design to drive organizational change, challenging outdated processes and building alignment across stakeholders. Proactively pushing through barriers to user-focused innovation and modeling a bias for action to unlock better outcomes for students and families within a complex federal environment.

Working hand-in-hand with product managers, engineers, policy experts, and contractors to ensure design decisions are fully integrated into development.

Mentoring others in human-centered and service design practices, elevating the organization's overall design maturity and building a culture that values design as essential to delivering public services that work for everyone.
Minimum Qualification Requirements You may meet the minimum qualifications for the GS-15, if you possess the specialize experience.

Specialized Experience for the GS-15 One year of experience in either federal or non-federal service that is equivalent to at least a GS-14 performing two (2) out of three (3) of the following duties or work assignments: 1.

Experience leading or serving in a senior role of a multi-disciplinary project involving the design, development, and implementation of a new system or a major enhancement to an existing IT system. 2. Experience serving as a design lead, overseeing adoption of new functionalities and/or technologies for users. 3.

Experience communicating technical concepts to non-technical audiences and translating business requirements into technical user stories.

Basic Experience Requirements: Applicants may qualify by meeting or exceeding the minimum proficiency level established for each of the required competencies, in addition to meeting the specialized experience requirement as demonstrated through the assessment of skills.

You must possess IT-related experience (paid or unpaid experience and/or completion of specific, intensive training (e.g., IT certification), as appropriate) demonstrating each of the nine competencies listed below. Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail.

Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (i.e., any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services.

Decision Making - Makes sound, well-informed, and objective decisions; perceives the impact and implications of decisions; commits to action, even in uncertain situations, to accomplish organizational goals; causes change.

Information Management - Identifies a need for and knows where or how to gather information; organizes and maintains information or information management systems.

Interpersonal Skills- Shows understanding, friendliness, courtesy, tact, empathy, concern, and politeness to others; develops and maintains effective relationships with others; may include effectively dealing with individuals who are difficult, hostile, or distressed; relates well to people from varied backgrounds and different situations.

Oral Communication- Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately.

Problem Solving- Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Teamwork- Encourages and facilitates cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit; works with others to achieve goals.

Technical Competence- Uses knowledge that is acquired through formal training or on-the-job experience to perform one's job; works with, understands, and evaluates technical information related to the job; advises others on technical issues.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs) The quality of your experience will be measured by the extent to which you possess the following knowledge, skills and abilities (KSAs).

You do not need to provide separate narrative responses to these KSAs, as they will be measured by your responses to the occupational questionnaire (you may preview the occupational questionnaire by clicking the link at the end of the Evaluations section of this vacancy announcement). Skill human-centered design and user experience methods.

Skill in service design and systems thinking. Skill in prototyping, testing, and iterating solutions at scale. Skill in navigating bureaucracy and driving design-led change. Ability to collaborate across disciplines and build a culture of design.

Individual Occupational Requirements: To qualify for this position, you must meet one of the Individual Occupational Requirements: Basic Requirements for Community Planning Series 0020: A.

Degree: Successful completion of a full 4-yr course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a bachelor's or higher degree that included a major field of study such as: community planning; or related field such as urban affairs, architecture, landscape architecture, engineering, sociology, geography, economics, political science, or public administration that included at least 12 semester hrs. in the planning process, socioeconomic & physical elements of planning, urban & regional economic analysis, & development finance.

Note: Applicants with degrees in related fields, such as those listed above, who do not have the 12 semester hrs. of specified course work must have had at least 1 yr. of work experience in community planning acquired under the supervision & guidance of a community planner. -OR- B.

Combination of Education & Experience: Courses equivalent to a major in one of the above disciplines, or a combination of related courses totaling at least 24 semester hrs. in any combination of the above disciplines of which at least 12 semester hrs. were in the planning process, & socioeconomic & physical elements of planning, plus appropriate experience or additional education.

Basic Requirements for General Engineering Series 0801: A. Degree: Successful completion of a full 4-year course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a bachelor's or higher degree in engineering.

To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential & integral calculus and courses in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields & circuits; (f) nature & properties of materials; & (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. -OR- B.

Combination of Education & Experience: College-level education, training, &/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, & (2) a good understanding, both theoretical & practical, of the engineering sciences & techniques & their applications to one of the branches of engineering.

The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: 1. Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT)1, or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico.

Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration.

For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions. 2.

Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE)2 examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico. 3.

Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, & engineering sciences & that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A.

The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A. 4.

Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance.

Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. Basic Requirements for Landscape Architecture Series 0807: A.

Degree: Successful completion of a full 4-year course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a bachelor's or higher degree in landscape architecture or landscape design. -OR- B.

Combination of Education & Experience: For each year short of graduation, the applicant must have had 1 yr of experience under professional leadership & guidance of such character & diversity as to be a satisfactory substitute for the required education.

This experience must have included original landscape design. ** See Education Section for additional qualification requirements**

To lead and deliver CAPEX investment and industrialization projects at the Haag site, ensuring efficient implementation from concept through completion. The role is critical in scaling and optimizing production processes, maximizing return on investment, and ensuring full compliance with safety, quality, and regulatory standards while supporting strategic business objectives.

* Lead and manage the implementation of CAPEX investment projects, ensuring alignment with site and business strategy.
* Drive industrialization initiatives to optimize, standardize, and scale production processes.
* Collaborate cross-functionally to analyze and improve workflows, ensuring efficient and sustainable process design.
* Ensure proper training and qualification of employees impacted by new or modified processes.
* Deliver projects within defined scope, budget, and timelines, maintaining transparency on cost and schedule performance.
* Monitor project progress, identify risks, and implement mitigation actions while ensuring compliance with safety, quality, and regulatory requirements.
* Prepare and present project updates, investment cases, and performance reports to stakeholders and senior management.
* Contribute to departmental improvement initiatives, driving efficiency and continuous improvement.

* Technical education in engineering or equivalent practical experience in an industrial environment, with a focus on production industrialization.
* Proven experience in managing CAPEX investment and process optimization projects.
* Solid understanding of Lean methodologies and process improvement tools.
* Strong analytical and structured thinking skills, particularly in industrialization and process design.
* Proficiency in German (spoken and written) and good command of English.
* Effective communication and collaboration skills across functions and teams.
* Ability to work independently and drive innovative solutions in a project-driven environment.
* Familiarity with Microsoft Dynamics 365 is an advantage.

Mener des initiatives de conception organisationnelle et de gestion du changement visant à renforcer l'efficacité opérationnelle, l'engagement des employés et la résilience organisationnelle.

Développer et mettre en œuvre des politiques, pratiques et initiatives en matière de ressources humaines alignées sur les valeurs, la culture et les objectifs stratégiques de PSI.

Superviser la prestation des opérations RH mondiales dans tous les sites de PSI, en garantissant cohérence, efficacité et conformité à la législation locale du travail et aux politiques organisationnelles.

Diriger et améliorer continuellement les processus liés au personnel, y compris le recrutement, l'intégration, la gestion du cycle de vie des employés, l'administration des contrats et la sortie des employés.

Assurer la conformité légale et réglementaire dans toutes les régions et bureaux pays, en atténuant les risques liés à l'emploi et en maintenant les meilleures pratiques RH. Gérer les systèmes RH mondiaux, les dossiers, les rapports et les analyses du personnel pour soutenir la prise de décisions éclairées.
**Gestion des talents & Développement des employés**
Diriger les processus mondiaux de planification des effectifs et de planification de la succession pour assurer la continuité organisationnelle et les capacités futures.

Développer et mettre en œuvre des initiatives d'apprentissage, de développement du leadership et de progression de carrière qui renforcent la performance organisationnelle et l'engagement des employés.

Superviser les processus de gestion de la performance, en veillant à ce que les managers soient équipés pour soutenir la haute performance et le développement professionnel. Promouvoir une culture d'apprentissage continu, de feedback et de responsabilité à travers l'organisation.

Promouvoir un lieu de travail diversifié, équitable, inclusif et psychologiquement sûr où tous les employés peuvent s'épanouir. Mener des initiatives liées au bien-être des employés, à la santé et sécurité, et au devoir de diligence dans tous les sites de PSI.

Fournir des conseils experts sur des questions complexes de relations avec les employés, la résolution de conflits et les enquêtes en milieu de travail lorsque nécessaire. Favoriser un dialogue social positif et un engagement constructif avec les représentants des employés et syndicats.

Coacher et conseiller les managers sur l'efficacité du leadership, les relations avec les employés, le développement des talents et le changement organisationnel. Permettre aux managers de prendre des décisions efficaces en matière de personnel grâce à des analyses basées sur les données et des conseils RH pratiques.

## Rejoins notre équipe tipee ! ##
Situés au cœur de Lausanne, nous sommes une PME d'une cinquantaine de collaboratrices et collaborateurs passionné-e-s. Nous développons tipee, une application de gestion du temps et portail RH qui simplifie la vie de nos clients depuis plus de 10 ans.
Fonctionnant en mode participatif et agile, notre société est organisée en cercles où chacun-e est autonome, avec son mot à dire et des possibilités d'évolution au sein de la boîte. Et cela, avec un impact positif pour nos clients, nos collègues, la communauté et l'environnement.
Pour renforcer notre organisation, nous cherchons un-e **People & Culture Manager**. Ce poste de cadre te place au cœur de l'humain chez tipee : tu veilles à ce que chacun-e soit soutenu-e et accompagné-e au quotidien, tu fais vivre l'équité et la cohérence de nos pratiques RH, et tu contribues activement à notre culture d'entreprise et à notre marque employeur.
Ce poste combine deux rôles : à titre principal, celui de **People & Culture Manager**, et à titre secondaire, celui de **facilitateur-trice** au sein de nos cercles.
## Ton rôle au quotidien ##
Tu fais partie de la direction et tu travailles en lien étroit avec l'ensemble des cercles et des coordinateurs-trices.
* Tu es **à l'écoute des besoins** des collègues et des coordinateurs-trices, et tu es la personne de référence pour tout sujet touchant à l'humain au sein de tipee.
* Tu accompagnes les cercles dans leurs **recrutements** : tu ne recrutes pas à leur place, tu les outilles pour qu'ils sachent le faire eux-mêmes, et tu les appuies pour optimiser chaque processus.
* Tu conçois et fais vivre un **onboarding et un offboarding formalisés**, pour que chaque nouvel-le arrivant-e soit bien accueilli-e et chaque départ bien accompagné, quel que soit le cercle.
* Tu accompagnes l'évolution professionnelle des collaborateurs-trices : entretiens annuels en duo lorsque nécessaire, discussions avec les personnes concernées, et une réflexion continue sur les **parcours et la mobilité interne**.
* En collaboration avec les cadres, tu gères les **situations difficiles** (résolution de tensions, recadrage, conflit, etc.), avec la discrétion et l'écoute que ces moments demandent.
* Tu participes à la **diversité, l'équité et l'inclusion (DEIB)** au sein de tipee, et tu veilles à ce que nos pratiques soient inclusives à chaque étape du parcours collaborateur-trice.
* Tu clarifies et fais vivre **nos bonnes pratiques** : rédaction de guides, conventions et chartes en duo avec la direction, et contribution aux réflexions sur notre culture d'entreprise lors des séances cadres.
* Tu portes le rôle de **facilitateur-trice** : animation de rituels et stimulation de l'intelligence collective au sein de nos cercles.
* Tu participes à l'**organisation et à l'animation** de nos journées annuelles au vert.
* Tu t'assures que nos **cercles et rôles** suivent l'évolution de nos équipes.
* Tu **représentes tipee** à l'externe, lors de conférences ou salons RH, et tu partages ainsi notre vision de l'humain au travail.
* Tu favorises le **partage de connaissances** en interne et l'amélioration continue de nos pratiques, notamment via le suivi de notre questionnaire eNPS.
## Ce qu'on recherche ##
* Une expérience confirmée dans un rôle très orienté vers l'humain "- People & Culture, coaching, facilitation, Scrum Master, ou fonction similaire.
* Une posture de coach : tu préfères outiller et responsabiliser les équipes plutôt que de faire à leur place.
* Une réelle capacité d'écoute, d'empathie et de discrétion, notamment dans les situations sensibles.
* Un esprit d'initiative et l'envie de faire évoluer nos pratiques.
* Une aisance avec la culture produit, l'agilité et la facilitation (animation de rituels, intelligence collective, gestion des tensions).
* Le goût de représenter une entreprise à l'externe et de créer des partenariats.
* Une bonne compréhension du fonctionnement en cercles et en rôles, ou l'envie de t'y investir pleinement.
* De bonnes connaissances RH sont un plus, mais ne sont pas une condition.
Tu n'as pas besoin d'avoir un parcours RH classique pour réussir dans ce rôle : ce n'est pas un poste d'administration du personnel. Ce qui compte avant tout, c'est ta capacité à accompagner les gens, à faciliter, à créer de la confiance et être un soutien.
## Travailler chez tipee ##
* **Flexibilité** : horaires modulables, travail hybride (jusqu'à 50% à distance), taux d'activité adaptable à l'évolution de ta vie personnelle.
* **Locaux à Lausanne** : à 15 minutes à pied de la gare, ou 7 en vélo ou trottinette.
* **Formation** : un budget individuel pour des conférences ou formations sur les sujets qui t'intéressent.
* **Culture participative** : entraide, dialogue, confiance, prise de responsabilités.
* **Engagements** : certifiée B Corp et STI, engagée sur les aspects sociétaux et environnementaux.
* **Mobilité** : jusqu'à CHF 300.- par année pour tes frais de transport durable (abonnement CFF).
* **Conditions** : des prestations LPP attractives auprès d'une caisse durable, des avantages autour du congé parental, au moins 5 semaines de vacances, et plus.
* **Vie d'entreprise** : événements réguliers et moments conviviaux qui rythment l'année.

Du dokumentierst alle Schritte und erstellst nach Projektende die Abschlussdokumentationen.

* Die Kapazitätsplanung sowie die Koordination mit externen Firmen oder Lieferanten fallen in dein Aufgabengebiet

* **Ausbildungen:** Kaufmännische oder technische Grundausbildung mit Weiterbildung zum Betriebsfachmann / Betriebstechniker (m/w/div.) oder eine höhere Fachausbildung in Maschinenbau / Betriebswirtschaft

We operate in a highly exciting, always time-critical and rapidly changing environment. Through intensive cooperation, we ensure transparency for the achievement of project goals and early identification of project risks. Nous accompagnons nos clients internationaux dans leurs innovations, les nouvelles technologies et transférons les développements produits vers la production en série et les autorisations. Pour renforcer notre équipe «Health & Life Sciences», nous recherchons votre profil.
### Domaine d-activité ###
En collaboration avec une équipe d-ingénierie qualifiée composée de scientifiques et de designers industriels, vous dirigez des développements étendus dans le domaine des applications médicales et des thérapies pharmaceutiques.

Vous conduisez l-équipe projet et êtes responsable des réalisations techniques ainsi que des applications des développements d-appareils et de systèmes utilisés par et pour les patients. Les connaissances spécialisées et une grande conscience de la qualité sont au cœur de votre travail quotidien.

Au sein de l-équipe projet, vous accompagnez les interlocuteurs internes et externes, de l-idée à la maturité série, pour des groupes internationaux, PME et start-ups.
Vous dirigez des équipes projet interdisciplinaires et internationales et travaillez en étroite collaboration avec nos collaborateurs et clients. Grâce à votre savoir, votre créativité et votre expérience, vous accompagnez les projets clients de la phase conceptuelle à la phase de design et de prototypage jusqu-à la vérification produit.

Votre enthousiasme et votre assurance vous aident à convaincre les clients de nos solutions. Vous pensez et agissez de manière entrepreneuriale, êtes résistant au stress et adoptez une méthode de travail pragmatique.

En raison des contacts internationaux et de la rédaction de documentation contrôlée, vous maîtrisez l-anglais à l-oral comme à l-écrit.
De plus, vous identifiez avec nos clients de nouveaux potentiels de développement et d-innovation, réalisez des analyses des besoins et contribuez activement au développement des relations stratégiques avec les clients ainsi qu-au développement commercial.

The Readiness & Response Team keeps Zoox's robotaxi fleet moving. Readiness prepares vehicles for service; Response protects the mission once vehicles are live — recovering vehicles, recovering riders, and coordinating incident response across every market we operate. When a robotaxi needs help on public roads, Response is what gets there, and our dispatchers are the nerve center that makes it happen.

As Program Manager, Response, you own the Response program end to end and lead the centralized dispatch team that runs it. You will not lead crews in the field — market leadership owns field execution.

You own dispatch, the recovery vendor network, the metric set, and the standards that make Response work the same way in Las Vegas as it does in Atlanta.

This is a builder's role in a program scaling toward a national footprint without scaling headcount at the same rate, and you will spend as much time designing how the work should be done as you will running it.

Lead the dispatch team: Manage, coach, and develop a team of Readiness and Response Dispatchers providing 24-hour coverage across all markets — including hiring, shift structure, scheduling, on-call rotation, and performance management.
Own Response program execution: Drive the four pillars of the program — vehicle recovery, rider recovery, incident response, and dispatch and oversight — across San Francisco, Foster City, Las Vegas, Austin, Miami, Los Angeles, and Atlanta, and stand the program up in each new market we launch.
Run the recovery vendor network: Hold third-party tow and rider recovery partners to their service levels through scorecards, escalation, and capacity planning, partnering with Logistics on contracts and Finance on cost per recovery.
Own the metrics: Define, instrument, and report the Response metric set — time to dispatch, dispatch to cleared scene, dispatch cancellation rate, recovery SLA attainment, recovery damage events, and cost per recovery — and use it to drive decisions rather than describe them.
Standardize the work: Support authoring and maintaining the workflows, escalation matrices, and management-of-change process that keep Response consistent across markets — build once, deploy everywhere.
Close the loop on incidents: Run post-incident retrospectives to a real standard — containment, solution, preventive action — and make sure the assigned actions actually land.
Partner across the stack: Work with Mission Control, GSOC, the Fusion Center, Safety, Product, and market leadership to remove the friction that shows up between the dispatch decision and the cleared scene.
Communicate up and out: Deliver the weekly Response update to leadership and represent the program in business reviews — TL;DR first, data-backed, no surprises.

Bachelor's degree in business management, operations, or a similar field discipline

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

Claude is used across government, from US federal civilian agencies to national security, state and local, and allied international governments, and nearly every model and product Anthropic ships has public sector work on the end of it.

Each of those segments runs under its own regulatory and deployment constraints, so delivering Claude to them means standing up compliant infrastructure with cloud partners, landing new models in restricted environments, bringing our application suite to parity with commercial, and clearing frameworks like FedRAMP, repeated for every segment.

We're hiring a Technical Program Manager to own that program.
Today that coordination is spread across the public sector product and engineering leads and the many teams they pull in: research, infrastructure, security, compliance, and product engineering. You'll become the single owner of that program, the person who knows where every workstream stands, what it is waiting on, and who needs to decide.

Over time, government customers get new models and products on a predictable cadence, authorizations like FedRAMP run as a steady program rather than a one-off push, and each new segment takes less bespoke effort than the last.

Own the program for delivering new Claude models into public sector environments: sequencing, dependencies, and tradeoffs across research, inference and capacity, cloud partners, safeguards, and compliance teams
Drive FedRAMP and similar authorization programs for Anthropic's public sector offerings, working with privacy, security, compliance, and platform engineering
Plan and sequence work across public sector segments, from model and API availability to application parity and segment-specific product work
Represent public sector requirements in model launch planning alongside the launch TPMs
Establish the operating rhythm: a single view of workstreams, owners, dependencies, risks, and status, with planning, escalation paths, and launch coordination across orgs
Convert recurring efforts into documented, repeatable processes so that each new segment or model requires less bespoke coordination

Have several years of experience in technical program management, with a track record of successfully delivering complex, cross-functional programs
Have shipped software or infrastructure into regulated or restricted environments (government clouds, air-gapped deployments, FedRAMP or similar authorization frameworks) and can engage meaningfully with the infrastructure, ML, and security engineers doing the work
Have experience coordinating across multiple engineering teams and organizations simultaneously, including research, security, and compliance partners
Are highly organized and can manage multiple parallel workstreams effectively across distributed teams
Thrive in unstructured environments with a knack for bringing order to chaos and creating clarity in ambiguous situations
Have excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence without authority
Have worked on public sector, defense, or government cloud programs, or hold or are eligible for a US security clearance (preferred but not required)
Are passionate about Anthropic's mission and interested in the challenges of bringing AI capabilities to public institutions safely and reliably
Are a US person. We have agreements with the US Government that mandate this for these roles.

How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles.

We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies.

Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request.

As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.
At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools.

Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up.

If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.
About the Department
The Infrastructure Engineering team builds and scales Cloudflare’s global network, ensuring high availability, security, and performance across hundreds of cities worldwide.

Within Infrastructure Engineering, the Hardware Integration Operations team acts as the critical bridge connecting our global manufacturing partners, procurement teams, and capacity strategy. We manage the end-to-end flow of server and network hardware into fully integrated data center racks to support our growing global network.

By working closely with external manufacturing partners and cross-functional teams, we ensure the infrastructure powering the internet is built, tested, and deployed efficiently, securely, and resiliently.

As a Senior Supply Chain Program Manager, you will own the integrated supply-planning interface connecting capacity demand, L10 hardware supply, and L11 rack integration.

In this senior individual contributor role, you will coordinate the transition of servers and network equipment from server-level manufacturing (L10) into complete rack integration (L11), providing global partners with the material readiness, capacity planning, and operational visibility needed to execute Cloudflare’s global expansion.

Drive Strategic Supply Planning: Connect capacity requirements with L10 hardware availability and L11 rack manufacturing schedules to maintain scalable supply plans across global regions.
Manage Material & Production Readiness: Oversee weekly supply allocation reporting, shortage reviews, and material-readiness assessments for upcoming rack integration builds.
Guide Operational Tradeoffs: Identify supply constraints and present actionable allocation options to Capacity Planning, evaluating tradeoffs between direct hardware shipping and complete rack integration.
Translate Long-Term Strategy: Convert quarterly and annual capacity forecasts into actionable operational requirements for L11 integration partners.
Monitor Program Financials & Progress: Track CapEx commitments against rack integration and deployment plans, giving leadership visibility into utilization, execution progress, and delivery risks.
Lead Supplier Relationships: Partner with global L11 integration providers through regular business reviews covering capacity, delivery, cost, quality, and performance.
Expand Resilient Manufacturing: Evaluate and recommend new L11 suppliers and build locations to strengthen geographic resiliency, capacity growth, and technical standards.
Support Commercial Operations: Validate supplier requisitions, purchase orders, and commercial agreements while supporting leadership approval workflows.
Partner on Global Supply Risk Mitigation: Collaborate with Capacity Planning, Procurement, and Hardware Sourcing to identify and mitigate rack integration risks involving capacity bottlenecks, logistics hurdles, tariffs, and regional concentration.
Partner on New Product Introductions (NPI): Collaborate with Hardware Engineering and rack integration teams to translate evolving hardware designs into operational preproduction and build readiness plans.
Support Supplier Quality: Analyze supplier-performance trends, coordinate escalations, and track cross-functional quality and engineering issues through resolution.
Operationalize ERP Workflows: Support adoption and stabilization of the team’s Oracle ERP processes, then identify improvements to planning, reporting, controls, and operational efficiency.
Deliver Executive Insights: Create clear forecasts, operational reporting, and risk assessments for leadership review.
Scale the Operating Model: Establish sustainable operational frameworks that expand production capacity while maximizing efficiency.

Discord has a highly engaged community of millions of daily active users who use the platform for many different reasons, but there’s one thing that nearly everyone does: play video games. Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming, and we are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to hang out before, during, and after playing games.
Creators are people who build audiences across the internet: influential voices whose communities listen to them and want to spend time together. Many of those communities already live on Discord, but our relationship with creators has grown organically. We have an opportunity to listen more closely, serve them more intentionally, and build a relationship that reflects the role they play on our platform.
We’re hiring a Senior Staff Program Manager to build Discord’s approach to creators from the ground up. You’ll begin with a selected group of creators already using Discord, build the fundamentals that serve them well, and develop programs that make their experience on Discord better.

Over time, you’ll turn what works into programs that can serve creators at scale and, eventually, give new creators more reasons to choose Discord. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who can lead through judgment, relationships, and execution.

You’ll report to the Director of Marketing, Player Communications and partner closely with Support, Product, Marketing, Communications, Partnerships, Policy, and more.
What You'll Be Doing
Build Discord’s creator strategy from the bottom up, starting with direct conversations and a clear understanding of what creators already on Discord need from us.
Bring together the creator work that exists across Discord today, establish clear ownership, and turn a collection of early efforts into a coherent program.
Define who we mean by creators and develop an initial approach for selecting and serving a trusted group across games, platforms, formats, and communities.
Create more than one program for creators, beginning with the fundamentals: accelerated support, clear paths for escalation, and reliable channels for two-way communication.
Manage relationships with important creators directly. Understand how they use Discord, help them solve meaningful problems, and build trust by following through.
Build a creator council or network that gives us a consistent view of what creators are seeing, where Discord is falling short, and what would make the platform more useful to them and their communities.
Build systems and playbooks that let a selected program grow over time without losing the relationships and responsiveness that made it valuable.
What you should have
A strong passion for Discord and/or gaming, and an appreciation for the creators and communities we serve.
7+ years in creator partnerships, community, platform programs, marketing, product partnerships, or a related field.
Deeply familiar with how creators build audiences, operate their businesses, and manage communities across platforms like YouTube, Twitch, TikTok, Instagram, Patreon, Reddit, and Discord.
You have built and operated creator or partner programs at scale, and you understand how to begin with a selected group without designing something that can never grow beyond it.
Biased to ship and iterate. You can launch a useful first version, learn from it, and raise the ambition over time.
Comfortable leading as an individual contributor. You create alignment and momentum across teams without relying on headcount or reporting lines.
An excellent cross-functional partner across Support, Product, Marketing, Comms, Partnerships, Policy, and more.

You have built a creator, partner, ambassador, advisory, or VIP program for a consumer platform.
You have designed accelerated support or escalation programs for influential users.
You have worked directly with gaming creators and understand the relationship between creators, games, and communities.
You have built programs involving product access, creator events, recognition, or discovery.
You have helped turn creator feedback into product changes, policies, or platform strategy.
You have built a program that began with a small trusted group and expanded without losing what made it valuable.

Klaviyo's infrastructure is the foundation that every product, every customer, and every engineer depends on. In this role you will be the connective tissue between our Infrastructure organization and the rest of engineering, driving the rollout of critical, cross-cutting programs that affect how we build, operate, and secure our platform at scale.
You will juggle a high volume of parallel efforts across cloud infrastructure, FinOps, build systems, software migrations, security operations, and more, keeping each moving, supporting teams to be successful, and escalating quickly when capacity or priority decisions need to be made. This is not a role for someone who waits to be told what to do. It's a role for someone who drives.
How you'll make a difference
Own the rollout of infrastructure initiatives across engineering. Drive programs from planning through completion, coordinating across teams that don't report to you and don't always have capacity to prioritize infrastructure work. Keep things moving.
Manage a high volume of concurrent efforts. At any given time you'll be tracking security operations improvements, FinOps initiatives, build system changes, software migrations, and other cross-cutting infrastructure programs simultaneously. Clear prioritization and status visibility are non-negotiable.
Hold teams accountable and escalate when needed. You know how to build the relationships and create the visibility that keeps infrastructure work from getting deprioritized. When a team genuinely lacks capacity, you surface that quickly, bring the right people into the conversation, and get a trade-off decision made — not absorb the delay quietly.
Develop a way to provide program health continuously. Establish and maintain clear, actionable reporting on the status of all infrastructure rollouts. Leadership should always know what's on track, what's at risk, and what decisions are needed from them.
Partner with Infrastructure leadership on planning and prioritization. Work closely with engineering and SRE leadership to build and maintain a rolling roadmap, sequence work across teams, and ensure infrastructure investments align with engineering and business priorities.
Define clear ways of working across teams. Create frameworks, templates, and coordination models that make it easier for infrastructure and product engineering teams to work together effectively. Build the playbook as you go.
Develop deep technical fluency in the programs you own. You don't need to write the code, but you need to understand what's being built, why it matters, and what the technical risks are well enough to ask the right questions, identify blockers early, and represent the work credibly to engineering leadership.
Drive automation and operational excellence. Challenge manual processes wherever you find them. Partner with infrastructure teams to identify opportunities to centralize and automate change rather than default to simply assigning out the same work to different teams.

Technically fluent. You've worked closely with infrastructure, SRE, or platform engineering teams. You understand security operations, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, and software migrations well enough to engage substantively, not just track status.
A driver, not a facilitator. You move work forward. You follow up, push back, escalate, and hold people accountable, constructively, but consistently. You don't wait for the next meeting to surface a problem.
Influential and relationship-driven. You know that infrastructure work gets done through trust, not authority. You build strong relationships across engineering teams, understand what motivates different stakeholders, and use that context to create alignment
AI-first in how you work. You don't just talk about AI, you use it daily to move faster, work smarter, and do more with less. You bring that mindset to the teams you work with and actively look for opportunities to automate, accelerate, and improve how programs are run.
Comfortable with high volume and ambiguity. You can manage many parallel workstreams without losing track of any of them, and you don't need a clean problem statement to get started.
Clear and direct communicator. You tailor your message by audience, engineering teams need different information than engineering VPs, and you make it easy for leadership to understand status and make decisions quickly.
Outcome-oriented. You measure success by realizing the impact and what improves, not by the quality of your tracking.

8+ years of experience in technical program management within a fast-paced product engineering environment, ideally SaaS or high-growth tech.
Demonstrated experience driving large-scale infrastructure rollouts across multiple engineering teams.
Familiarity with cloud infrastructure, FinOps, security operations, and software migration programs.
Strong fluency in tools such as Jira, Linear, Asana, or Smartsheet.
Track record of managing competing priorities and delivering results without direct authority over engineering teams.

Experience in both infrastructure and product engineering contexts.
Familiarity with FinOps frameworks and cloud cost optimization programs.
Experience building or evolving TPM practices in a nascent or growing function.
Hands-on with CI/CD tooling, build systems, or security compliance frameworks.

Team & Role
Moveworks, now part of ServiceNow, is building the agentic AI layer that sits between every employee and the systems they rely on. Following the acquisition, the Moveworks Business Unit is one of the most strategically important investments at ServiceNow — and the scope of what we own is expanding fast.

We are looking for a Director-level Technical Program Manager (Individual Contributor) to lead our most critical programs end to end, starting with the ServiceNow integration and growing into a broader portfolio over time as the BU scales.
This is a senior, highly technical IC role for someone who has spent most of their career running infrastructure, platform modernization, or large-scale distributed systems programs. You will manage the program — directly, end to end — and your influence will come from technical depth, sharp judgment, and an ability to align engineering leaders, executives, and partner organizations around a single execution plan. As the Moveworks BU scope expands, so will yours.

s.h: What you get to do in this role
s.t:
Own the Moveworks Infrastructure portfolio of strategic and technical initiatives. Your primary focus will be to drive the roadmap and execution plans for Moveworks Infrastructure initiatives; as you scale you will also take over from engineering infra operational processes like capacity planning and budgeting
Focus on initiatives expanding MW Infra footprint . We are moving to a tri-cloud + on-prem + SPC strategy where we need to develop the tools and process for managing our infra stack across diverse environments. Align any ambiguous strategic direction into concrete milestones, dependencies, and decision points.
Run the program, not the people . As the TPM, you will be the connective tissue across engineering, product, design, security, GTM, finance, and field organizations — driving outcomes through clarity, structured decision-making, and relentless follow-through.
Identify and resolve technical misalignment . Spot misalignment across teams, architectures, and roadmaps early — before it becomes a delivery risk — and partner with engineering leads to drive resolution quickly. Lead architecture reviews, surface cross-system risks (latency budgets, blast radius, multi-tenancy, AI safety, evals), and broker tradeoffs between engineering teams.
Build the operating system for the program . Status, risk, scope, and decision logs that engineering directors and VPs actually read. Quarterly planning rhythms that reflect reality. Executive narratives that are honest about where things stand.
Be the senior partner to engineering leadership . Pair directly with Distinguished Engineers, VPs of Engineering, and product leaders. Represent the program to the CTO, CPO, and executive staff. Own the message.
Define TPM excellence . As we grow and expand our TPM team, you will serve as the model for how to operate. Set the standard for what senior technical program management looks like at Moveworks, mentor TPMs across the org without being their manager, and codify the patterns that scale.

12+ years of technical program management experience, with most of that time spent on infrastructure, platform, cloud, reliability, developer productivity, or modernization programs. You have operated at staff, principal, or director IC scope on programs where the hard part was not coordination alone, but understanding technical dependencies, sequencing migrations, managing reliability risk, and helping engineering leaders make durable tradeoffs.
Deep technical fluency across infrastructure modernization domains — distributed systems, cloud-native infrastructure, Kubernetes, multi-region and multi-cloud architectures, hyperscaler platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP), identity, data platforms, observability, reliability, and migration strategy. You do not need to be the architect, but you need enough technical depth to pressure-test plans, spot cross-system risk, and earn credibility with senior engineers.
A track record of leading cross-org programs involving 100+ engineers, multiple VPs, and competing roadmaps — ideally including at least one large-scale integration, migration, or platform unification.
Excellent written communication. You can compress a 200-engineer program into a one-page exec narrative without losing the truth of it. You write decision docs that hold up under scrutiny.
Strong technical judgment under ambiguity. You know when to dig in, when to delegate to engineering leads, and when to escalate. You are comfortable saying “this plan won’t work” in a room full of senior leaders.

Prior IC senior TPM experience at a hyperscaler, large SaaS platform, or AI-first company.
Comfort operating across SaaS, on-prem regulated, and government cloud (FedRAMP, IL5) deployment models.
Experience leading post-acquisition technical integration programs at scale.
Background in agentic AI, conversational AI, or AI assistant platforms — you understand why agent runtimes, tool calling, RAG, and evals are not the same problem.

s.h: What Success Looks Like in the First Year
s.t:
Quarter 1: You have a grasp of the Moveworks replatform roadmap and are driving the execution plan for the first release helping the team address blockers. Engineering leaders across ServiceNow and Moveworks trust your judgment and pull you into the rooms that matter.
Quarter 2: You are able to scale to drive multiple releases going on in parallel on the Moveworks replatforming roadmap as well as the current infrastructure expansion and improvement initiatives, and proactively surface key risks to the plans and drive the path to mitigation. The executive staff has confidence in the plan because the plan is honest.
Quarter 3-4: Team has successfully delivered 1 or 2 releases on the roadmap under your leadership; major milestones land on time and at quality, and you are a trusted partner for infrastructure leadership and team

This role is especially compelling for senior TPMs who have operated in high-scale infrastructure environments and want more ownership than a narrowly-scoped platform program can offer. You will get the scale, technical complexity, and executive visibility of a large technology company, combined with the pace, ambiguity, and scope expansion of a fast-growing AI business unit.
Most senior TPM roles come with a fixed scope and focus on driving meetings and reporting the status. This one is different. It is a seat at the center of the Moveworks BU which is growing at an unprecented rate — your scope will expand as the BU scales. You will be measured by the technical and business outcomes you drive. If you thrive in an environment where you have the agency to move the needle for the company and learn something new every single day, then this role is for you.

个人信息及目的：你的如下个人信息将被处理并用于招聘：姓名、电子邮箱、电话号码、所在地区、经验和教育信息、简历等应聘者自主提交的附件信息、证件号、职位、部门、计划入职日期、劳动合同持续时间、工作地点、月薪、年薪、浮动奖金比例、餐贴、车贴。 博世将依据相关的数据保护法规，在全球范围内对您的数据进行保密。招聘流程中，您的个人信息只有在必须时才会被提供给博世以外的第三方机构(如代理机构)。博世精心挑选了第三方机构并与之签订了保密合同。博世采取了种种保密措施以保护您的数据，确保其不会遭受操纵、丢失、破坏、未经授权的访问或泄漏。我们的安全措施将随着新技术的应用而不断升级。您的本地浏览器和我们的人才招募系统之间的数据传输通过https加密。 特定职位申请：申请博世集团的职位就意味着您将自己的个人信息提供给博世集团旗下相应的法律实体（具体请见博世集团法人清单）。请注意，若有任何文件或资料变更，请在所有申请书里一并变更。人力资源部门的员工可能与您联系，询问您是否同意将您的求职申请转向博世集团内部另一合适职位。如果您申请了特定职位，那么只有在您同意的情况下，博世才会将您的求职申请转向另一职位。 您可以随时撤回求职申请，博世将根据相关法律删除您的个人信息。与您的申请相关的所有资料将被保留至24个月。您的权利：若您希望停止向博世提供您的个人信息，可联系我们或通过博世网上招聘数据隐私声明中的BKMS系统提出申请。您可以在SmartRecruiters平台查阅和修改您的简历。您对您的个人信息的处理享有知情权、决定权，您有权限制或者拒绝我们对您的个人信息进行处理。您还可以更正、补充您的个人信息。 跨境传输：为了实现前述目的，我们所收集的您的个人信息可能会在多个国家或地区间进行跨境转移，例如德国、新加坡。 德国：罗伯特-博世有限公司（德国格宁根市罗伯特博世广场1号（Robert-Bosch-Platz 1, Gerlingen-Schillerhohe, Germany，邮编：70839），用于集团统一招聘管理（博世中国与数据接收方均基于该目的开展数据出境活动； 英国：SmartRecruiters（英国伯克郡温莎亚瑟路圣斯蒂芬大厦 邮政区码: SL4 1RU），用于招聘、后期交流联系及分享职位/活动信息、潜在人才社区邀请。 您可通过上述联系方式依法向境外接收方行使您在个人信息处理活动中的权利。 存储您的个人信息：我们将仅在为实现目的必要的范围内以及法律法规要求的时间内保留您的个人信息。 雇佣：被雇佣后，您提供的数据将被从当前招聘系统转移至职位所属公司的人力资源管理系统。联系方式： 请通过访问博世中国官方主页：博世在中国＞加入博世＞工作机会，在网上招聘数据隐私声明中“9.联系方式” 博世集团法人清单： 请通过访问博世中国官方主页：博世在中国＞加入博世＞工作机会，在网上招聘数据隐私声明中获取现阶段使用网上招聘系统的博世集团法人（第五页）

Business Operations, Compliance & Audits
PMI Project Management: Take ownership of PMI projects assigned by BV.
IP Management.
Export Control & Compliance: Execute and monitor export control processes to ensure Hub operations comply with international and internal export control regulations.
RBA System Maintenance: Implement and maintain RBA (Responsible Business Alliance) standards, promoting responsible corporate operational practices.
Audit Leadership & Coordination: Lead and coordinate Internal System Audits and Customer Audits. Responsible for pre-audit preparation, on-site coordination, and tracking the closure of post-audit corrective actions.
IT , Administrative Facility Management and Culture Initiatives
Manage office IT infrastructure and enforce data security. Oversee daily administrative services and facility management to ensure smooth Hub operations. Drive and execute culture promotion initiatives to enhance employee engagement.

Bachelor's degree or above in Engineering, Management, Compliance or related fields.
Experience
Relevant experience in Project Management, Engineering, PRM/PJM, Compliance or Quality .
Experience in cross-functional project management and audit coordination preferred.
Skills
Strong project management, stakeholder management and execution skills.
Ability to work independently and influence stakeholders across functions.
Strong organizational and problem-solving skills.
Language
Excellent English skills
